Comment: Kali quantum task pipeline (account 060274391988, region us-east-2): validate a circuit against a local/Braket simulator, pause for an explicit human approval (SNS + waitForTaskToken), then submit to a real Braket QPU only once approved. See aws/step-functions/README.md before deploying this - several placeholders below need real values from your account, and there is no free/local equivalent for Stage 3: a real quantum device task costs real money the moment it runs.

ValidateCircuit.Comment: Runs the circuit against a local/Braket simulator first - the SAME kind of validation Kali's existing run_quantum_circuit chat tool already does (see app/api/ai-one-chat/route.ts), just invoked as a state machine step instead of a chat tool call. This calls out to that same external Python/Braket microservice (Vercel's Node runtime can't run Braket's SDK directly) - REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KALI_VALIDATION_SERVICE_ENDPOINT below with its real, reachable URL. That service must return qubitCount, estimatedCostUsd, and circuitSummary in its response body for the approval notification below to have real numbers in it - if it doesn't already return those fields, they need to be added there (that service isn't part of this repo, so it isn't something this change could add for you).

ValidationFailed.Cause: The circuit failed local-simulator validation before ever reaching the approval/QPU stages - no cost was incurred.

RequestApproval.Comment: Pauses here until POST /api/kali/approve-task calls SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure against $$.Task.Token - that route is the only thing that can move this forward. TimeoutSeconds below (24h) is a starting point, not a fixed requirement - tune it to how quickly you expect a human to actually respond.

Message.default.$: States.Format('Kali quantum task pending approval: {} qubits, target {}, est. ${}. Approve or reject via the dashboard.', $.validation.qubitCount, $.targetQpu, $.validation.estimatedCostUsd)

ApprovalTimedOut.Cause: No approval decision arrived within the timeout window - no QPU task was ever submitted, no cost was incurred.

ApprovalRejected.Cause: An approver explicitly rejected this task via POST /api/kali/approve-task - no QPU task was ever submitted, no cost was incurred.

ExecuteOnQpu.Comment: The only state in this whole machine that spends real money - everything above it exists specifically to gate this one call behind an explicit human decision. DeviceArn/Shots/Action come from the original input ($.targetQpu / $.shots / $.circuitPayload), not hardcoded here, since 'target QPU' is meant to vary per request. REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_BRAKET_RESULTS_BUCKET below with a real S3 bucket you own in this account/region.
